**Publish gate report: landing hero**

**Going out:** Landing page hero, Pebblebrook Tea Co., UK audience.

**Claims check**
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Good tea" | Opinion, fine |
| "guaranteed" | Not on the policy list. The policy only backs "pause or cancel any time". No guarantee of any kind is listed. |
| "Risk-free" | Not on the policy list. No money-back or trial terms are on record, so this is unproven. |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | On the policy list |
| "packed by hand in Bristol" | On the policy list ("every tin is packed by hand in Bristol") |
| "free UK delivery on orders over £25" | On the policy list |

**Regulated claims:** "Guaranteed" and "risk-free" are offer and refund-type claims. Under UK advertising rules, a guarantee needs its terms stated or easily accessible, and "risk-free" implies the customer can't lose money. Neither is supported here.

**House style:** The opening "Good tea, guaranteed." is a slogan-style line, and the copy is otherwise plain and specific. No banned words are given in the policy. Fine once the guarantee wording is removed.

**Disclosure:** This is the brand's own page, with no sponsorship, affiliate link or AI-realistic imagery. Nothing to label.

**Fixed (suggested rewrite):**
> Good tea, simply. Certified organic by the Soil Association, packed by hand in Bristol, and free UK delivery on orders over £25.

If you want to keep a risk-reducing message, the policy backs this: "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time."

**Needs a decision:**
1. If Pebblebrook does offer a real guarantee or money-back policy, add its terms to the brand policy (or give me the source here), and I'll reinstate the wording with a link to the terms.
2. Approver: the policy names no approver, so the yes needs to come from you. I haven't recorded any approval. Please confirm the rewritten copy before it goes out.

**Verdict:** Not ready to publish as drafted.
